assertions: Sir William Waller and the Parliamentarian side overcome: Waller wins the engagement near Alresford (Battle of Cheriton) on the day of the question, 29 March 1644, and Hopton loses the field

Waller's significators are decisively the stronger: Ascendant and Moon together with Jupiter and Venus, and the Moon in her exaltation with Jupiter, give Waller's army fortune, strength and growing momentum

Sir Ralph Hopton himself and his Royalist army are debilitated: Saturn, lord of the 7th for Hopton, is in his fall, peregrine, sub radiis (under the Sun's beams), in no aspect to any planet, yet squaring the cusp of the 7th — a commander hidden, unsupported and afflicted

Assistance and substance favour Waller, not Hopton: the Sun, lord of Waller's substance/assistants, is angular in the 10th in the very degree of his exaltation (19° Aries), denoting powerful, honourable help ready for Waller

Hopton has no supplies/second help ready: nothing benefic supports his side, only Mars and the South Node occupy the relevant house — his supplies and reserves are lacking or harmful rather than forthcoming

The Moon, swift in motion and increasing in light and 11° distant from Venus, shows Waller's fortune swiftly increasing towards victory, while Hopton is forced to retreat/give ground rather than prevail
method: Lilly classical horary astrology for battle questions (1st house/Ascendant side vs 7th house opponent, essential and accidental dignity, exaltation/fall, sub radiis, angularity and benefic/malefic assistance)
reasoning: Querent/Waller side taken by Ascendant, Moon, Jupiter and Venus; opponent Hopton by Saturn lord of 7th. Moon exalted and with Jupiter (great benefic) strengthens Waller; Sun lord of Waller's 2nd/substance in 10th at exact exaltation degree gives strong, honourable assistants. Conversely Saturn in fall, peregrine, sub radiis, unaspected and squaring 7th cusp debilitates Hopton; Mars + South Node alone where his help should be shows no supplies ready. Swift Moon increasing in light confirms growing advantage to Waller, hence a clear, same-day Waller victory.
summary: Waller overcomes Hopton at Cheriton — Waller's side is exalted, angular and well-assisted, Hopton's significator fallen, peregrine and unsupported with no supplies ready.
